questions.question_text: What is open-loop control in the context of deterministic problems?
questions.answer: Um, so, open-loop control in deterministic problems, like, basically means you just give a sequence of actions without worrying about the feedback. It's, like, super straightforward because you can predict everything, right? So, you just choose the best actions ahead of time, and then, you know, just let it run without checking back. It’s kind of like, um, setting your alarm clock and not looking at it again until the morning. You totally don’t need to optimize anything because it’s all predetermined. So, yeah, it’s basically just doing what you planned without any adjustments.
